egress.answer: YES for two rootless mechanisms; NO for any firewall-based approach

egress.self_test_result: SELF-TEST: PASS -- every mechanism behaved as its label claims. Both positive controls (host, docker-bridge) were OPEN and all three negative controls were BLOCKED, with local=ok on docker-internal proving the barrier is selective rather than broken networking.
egress.real_connection_attempt_evidence: logs/egress_cmd_demo.log: the same runtime command (urllib.request.urlopen https://example.com) printed 'RUNTIME EGRESS SUCCEEDED: 200' on the host and 'RUNTIME EGRESS FAILED: URLError' inside unshare -rn
sharp_edges: A new network namespace has its OWN loopback: `unshare -rn` + `ip link set lo up` works, but the host's 127.0.0.1 services are NOT reachable (measured: postgres on 127.0.0.1:5432 -> OSError Errno 101 Network is unreachable).
`docker --internal` likewise has no route to the host; local services must be SIBLINGS on the same internal network (proven reachable by container name).

Consequence for KAPSO: only the lane's candidate-execution channel can be wrapped; the orchestrator that talks to the model endpoint must stay outside the barrier. This matches the design anyway, since the orchestrator legitimately needs model access.
Section 4.3's 'Codex CLI workspace-write defaults to network_access:false' could NOT be tested end-to-end because codex cannot complete any call on this machine (see cli_login.codex).
environment_quirks: http_proxy/https_proxy are set to http://127.0.0.1:7890 (mihomo/Clash Meta, PID 608, tun0 interface 10.8.0.106/24 up); the proxy BREAKS some hosts (curl https://pypi.org/simple/ via proxy -> 000/timeout, direct -> 200).

Raw TCP to some public IP literals times out even though the host is online: 1.1.1.1:443, 8.8.8.8:443, 9.9.9.9:443 all time out; 1.1.1.1:80, 8.8.8.8:53 and example.com:443 by name connect. The canary therefore tries several targets and reports tcpvia=<which worked>.
The canary uses --noproxy '*': a probe must measure the context's own egress, not a relay the host has configured.
Adapter guidance: run network-touching installs with the proxy unset, or pypi/npm may fail even though the network is fine.

resources.assessment: One Postgres (~150-250MB) plus one Redis (~10MB) are negligible. Several concurrent agent runtimes are feasible; the binding constraint is CPU (12 threads) and model-endpoint network latency, not memory or disk.

bottom_line: Infrastructure prerequisites (interpreters, dependency resolution, container infra, egress closure, resources) are all satisfied. The blocker is model access: with codex unable to complete any call, only SimpleLoop is guaranteed runnable today, and the A0 rule |R_1| >= 1 would reduce A0 to the baseline. Restoring the relay on 127.0.0.1:15722 and confirming claude are the two highest-value fixes before the adapters are written.
